name: 26440-longdecode-dsv2lite16b-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), SM90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, EP off. One in-process vLLM engine, one process.
architecture: MoE decoder, DeepseekV2ForCausalLM, 27 layers, multi-head latent attention, bf16 -- all readable off the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=32, bounded at 256 requests, first 25% by completion discarded as warmup, 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt exactly 256 tokens and output exactly 1024 (min = max on both, ignore_eos), so every request is the same fixed shape.
purpose: A long-form content generator for writers, producing 1024-token drafts from short prompts for 32 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. Every key must be top-level and every value must fit on ONE line:
# the reader takes this file line by line and skips indented ones, so re-flowing a structured
# value into a block mapping drops the key silently and the engine starts without it.

model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat

# The checkpoint ships `configuration_deepseek.py` and an `auto_map`, so the config loads whether
# or not the installed transformers knows `model_type: deepseek_v2`.
trust-remote-code: true

tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# Far above the 256 + 1024 this workload needs, so it never binds; it caps the KV allocation
# instead of letting the checkpoint's 163840-token rope window size it.
max-model-len: 8192

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# Written down rather than left to resolve: the engine's own defaults for these two vary with the
# usage context it is constructed under, and these are the served-deployment values.
max-num-seqs: 1024
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
